definition_en: to repair something, to solve a problem, to fasten something in place, or to decide something firmly
core_image: 拧紧松动的螺丝，让摇晃的椅子重新站稳
scene: 他花了一下午修好了那把摇晃的椅子。He spent the afternoon fixing the wobbly chair.
sceneCN: 这里 fix 是「修理」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他花了一下午修好了那把摇晃的椅子。

senses.title: Repair
senses.definition: to make something whole or working again
senses.definitionCN: 使某物恢复完整或正常运转
senses.example: He fixed the wobbly chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他修好了那把摇晃的椅子。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of fixing a broken object.
senses.whyCN: 这是修理损坏物品时最日常的义项。

senses.title: Solve
senses.definition: to find a solution to a problem
senses.definitionCN: 为问题找到解决办法
senses.example: They fixed the problem in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一小时就解决了问题。
senses.why: A problem is treated like a machine that needs repair.
senses.whyCN: 问题被当作需要修理的机器来对待。

senses.title: Fasten
senses.definition: to attach something firmly in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定在某个位置
senses.example: The shelf is fixed to the wall with screws.
senses.exampleCN: 架子用螺丝固定在墙上。
senses.why: The oldest sense is driving something in until it cannot move.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是把东西钉进去使其不能移动。

senses.title: Arrange firmly
senses.definition: to decide or arrange something definitely
senses.definitionCN: 把某事明确地决定或安排好
senses.example: We fixed a date for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 我们确定了会议的日期。
senses.why: Something fixed is no longer open to change.
senses.whyCN: 被固定下来的事就不再变动了。

intro.en: Fix comes from Latin figere, to fasten or drive in, through its participle fixus.
intro.cn: fix 源自拉丁语 figere（钉住、固定），经其分词 fixus 进入英语。

items.en: Figere meant to drive in or fasten.
items.cn: figere 意为钉入或固定。

items.en: The participle fixus meant fastened or fixed.
items.cn: 分词 fixus 意为被固定住的。

items.en: Fixare meant to fasten or settle something.
items.cn: fixare 意为使固定、使确定。

items.en: Fix named fastening and then repairing.
items.cn: fix 先指固定，后指修理。

items.en: The word also came to mean solving or arranging.
items.cn: 这个词又引申为解决或安排。

note.en: Fix is compared with similar-looking words and with words for repair and fastening.
note.cn: 把 fix 与形近词以及表示修理和固定的词作比较。

entries.definition: a wild animal with a bushy tail
to repair a hole or tear

normalIntro.en: Fix means to make firm: you fasten it, then you make it work again.
normalIntro.cn: fix 的核心是「使牢固」：先固定，再让它恢复正常。

normal.en: You fix a broken chair.
You fix a problem at work.
You fix a shelf to the wall.
You fix a date for a trip.
A fixed price never changes.

abstract.en: To fix is to stop something from shaking.
abstract.cn: 修理就是让某物不再摇晃。

abstract.en: A fixed point makes movement measurable.
abstract.cn: 固定的参照点让运动可以被衡量。

abstract.en: Some things are easier to fix than to explain.
abstract.cn: 有些东西修起来比解释起来容易。

examples.en: Can you fix the leaking tap?
examples.cn: 你能修一下漏水的水龙头吗？

examples.en: They fixed the date for the wedding.
examples.cn: 他们确定了婚礼的日期。

examples.en: The mirror is fixed to the wall.

dict_mnemonic.text: fix 源自拉丁语 figere（钉住），本义「固定」，故障被「固定」回正常状态就是修理。

root: 源自拉丁语 figere（钉入、固定），核心义「使牢固不动」。

sensesIntro.en: Fix means to repair, to solve, to fasten, or to settle something firmly.
sensesIntro.cn: fix 意为修理、解决、固定或把某事确定下来。

core.en: To make something firm and no longer loose.
core.cn: 使某物牢固、不再松动。

branches.en: A broken thing made whole again.
branches.cn: 把损坏的东西恢复完整。

branches.en: A problem settled like a loose part.
branches.cn: 像拧紧零件一样解决问题。

branches.en: An object held firmly in place.
A decision made firm and final.
branches.cn: 把决定敲定得稳固而最终。

branches.en: Repair and fastening share the idea of firmness.
branches.cn: 修理与固定共享「牢固」这一概念。

intro.en: Fix belongs to a Latin family built on figere, to fasten.
intro.cn: fix 属于以拉丁语 figere（固定）为核心构建的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin figere and its participle fixus supply the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 figere 及其分词 fixus 提供了整个词族。

items.example: He fixes cars for a living.
He fixated on one small detail.
items.exampleCN: 他盯住一个小细节不放。

latinEntries.example: The Latin verb figere meant to fasten.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语动词 figere 意为固定。

latinEntries.example: Fixus is the participle of figere.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fixus 是 figere 的分词。

definition_en: a piece of cloth used as a symbol or signal, to mark something for attention, or to become weak and tired
core_image: 风里一面旗子啪啦啪啦地抖，布面朝一个方向翻卷
scene: 一面红旗在楼顶迎风飘扬。A red flag waved on the roof.
sceneCN: 这里 flag 是「旗」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一面红旗在楼顶迎风飘扬。

senses.title: Banner
senses.definition: a piece of cloth that stands for a country or group
senses.definitionCN: 代表国家或团体的布制标志
senses.example: A red flag waved on the roof.
senses.why: This is the basic and most familiar sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基础也最熟悉的义项。

senses.title: Mark
senses.definition: to mark something so that people notice it
senses.definitionCN: 做出标记以便人们注意到某事物
senses.example: The editor flagged the error in red.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑用红色标出了错误。
senses.why: A small flag marks a place, and so does a note.
senses.whyCN: 小旗标记位置，标记符号也起同样作用。

senses.title: Grow weak
senses.definition: to become tired, weak, or less active
senses.definitionCN: 变得疲倦、虚弱或不再活跃
senses.example: His energy flagged after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行后他的精力衰退了。
senses.why: The cloth of a flag droops when the wind dies.
senses.whyCN: 风停时旗布会耷拉下来，正如精力消退。

senses.title: Nation symbol
senses.definition: the cloth symbol of a country
senses.definitionCN: 代表一个国家的布制象征
senses.example: The flag flew at half-mast.
senses.why: The banner sense became a fixed symbol of the state.
senses.whyCN: 旗帜义固定为国家的象征。

intro.en: The origin of flag is uncertain; it appears in late Middle English as a word for cloth.
intro.cn: flag 的来源不确定，中古英语晚期以「布」的意思出现。

items.en: The noun may echo the flapping sound of cloth.
items.cn: 这个名词可能模仿布匹拍打的声音。

items.en: Flagge named a piece of cloth hung as a signal.
items.cn: flagge 指悬挂作信号的一块布。

items.en: Flag came to mean a national or military banner.
items.cn: flag 进而指国旗或军旗。

items.en: The verb flagged came to mean marking for attention.
items.cn: 动词 flagged 意为做标记以引起注意。

items.en: Another verb sense means to grow weak or tired.
items.cn: 另一动词义项意为变得虚弱或疲倦。

note.en: Flag is compared with similar-looking words and with words for banners and signs.
note.cn: 把 flag 与形近词以及表示旗帜和标志的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flag or badge of a group

normalIntro.en: Flag is first a cloth in the wind; later it marks a spot and then droops with tiredness.
normalIntro.cn: flag 先是风中的一块布，后来用来标记位置，再引申为精力萎顿。

normal.en: A flag flies above the school.
She flagged the page with a note.
normal.cn: 她用便条标记了那一页。

normal.en: His interest flagged after an hour.
normal.cn: 一小时后他的兴趣减退了。

normal.en: The flag was lowered at sunset.
Red flags warn of danger.

abstract.en: A flag gives a crowd one shape to look at.
abstract.cn: 旗帜给人群一个共同的注视对象。

abstract.en: To flag something is to say: look here.
abstract.cn: 标记某物就是在说：看这里。

abstract.en: Energy, like cloth, falls when the wind stops.
abstract.cn: 精力如布，风停便垂落。

examples.en: A red flag waved on the roof.
The editor flagged the error in red.
examples.cn: 编辑用红色标出了错误。

examples.en: His energy flagged after the long walk.
examples.cn: 长途步行后他的精力衰退了。

dict_mnemonic.text: flag 可能模仿布匹拍打声，本义「一块布」，用作旗，再引申为标记与「像旗一样垂落」的变弱。

root: 来源不确定，中古英语 flagge 指一块悬垂的布，核心画面是「风中飘动的布」。

sensesIntro.en: Flag means a banner, a mark for attention, a national symbol, or to grow weak.
sensesIntro.cn: flag 意为旗帜、标记、国旗象征，或变得虚弱。

core.en: A cloth that signals or marks.
core.cn: 用来发出信号或作标记的布。

branches.en: A cloth lifted by the wind.
A mark that draws the eye.
Strength drooping like still cloth.
branches.cn: 力量像静止的布一样垂落。

branches.en: The cloth that stands for a country.
Signal and mark grow from the same cloth.
branches.cn: 信号与标记都源于同一块布。

intro.en: Flag is a Germanic word that builds compounds with poles, ships, and stone.
intro.cn: flag 是日耳曼语词，能与旗杆、船只和石板构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Flag has no Latin ancestor; Latin vexillum, a small banner, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flag 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 vexillum（小旗）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 他低落的情绪又高涨起来。

items.meaning: a pole that holds a flag

items.example: The path is made of flagstone.

items.meaning: a person who carries a flag

definition_en: the hot glowing gas of a fire, a strong feeling of passion, or to burn brightly
core_image: 烛芯顶端一跳一跳的橙色火舌
scene: 蜡烛的火苗在风里摇得很厉害。The flame of the candle shook in the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 flame 是「火焰」（第 1 个义项）；句意：蜡烛的火苗在风里摇得很厉害。

senses.title: Burning gas
senses.definition: the bright burning gas that rises from a fire
senses.definitionCN: 从火中升起的明亮燃烧气体
senses.example: The flame of the candle shook in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 蜡烛的火苗在风里摇晃。
senses.why: This is the physical sense seen every day.
senses.whyCN: 这是每天都能看到的物理义项。

senses.title: Fire
senses.definition: fire, especially when it is burning strongly
senses.definitionCN: 火，尤指燃烧猛烈时
senses.example: Dry wood burst into flames.
senses.why: The plural flames often names a whole fire.
senses.whyCN: 复数 flames 常指一整片火。

senses.title: Passion
senses.definition: a strong feeling of love or enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 强烈的爱意或热情
senses.example: The flame of ambition still burned in her.
senses.exampleCN: 她心中雄心之火仍在燃烧。
senses.why: Heat became a metaphor for strong feeling.
senses.whyCN: 热度被隐喻为强烈的情感。

senses.title: To burn
senses.definition: to burn with bright flames
senses.definitionCN: 冒出明亮火焰地燃烧
senses.example: The logs flamed in the fireplace.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb of burning.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示燃烧的动词。

intro.en: Flame goes back through Old French to Latin flamma, a flame, from flare, to blow.
intro.cn: flame 经古法语上溯到拉丁语 flamma（火焰），源于 flare（吹）。

items.en: Flamma meant a flame or blazing fire.
items.cn: flamma 意为火焰或熊熊烈火。

items.en: The verb flare meant to blow or puff.
items.cn: 动词 flare 意为吹气、喷出。

items.en: Flambe carried the word into French.
items.cn: flambe 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Flame named the burning gas of fire.
items.cn: flame 指火中燃烧的气体。

items.en: The word also became a metaphor for passion.
items.cn: 这个词也成为激情的隐喻。

note.en: Flame is compared with similar-looking words and with words for fire and light.
note.cn: 把 flame 与形近词以及表示火与光的词作比较。

entries.definition: burning that gives heat and light

normalIntro.en: Flame is the visible tongue of fire, and by metaphor the heat of feeling.
normalIntro.cn: flame 是火可见的舌头，也比喻感情的炽热。

normal.en: A candle burns with a small flame.
The house was in flames.
The flame of love can fade.
The logs flamed brightly.
An old flame is a former lover.

abstract.en: A flame needs fuel, air, and a beginning.
abstract.cn: 火焰需要燃料、空气和一个开端。

abstract.en: Heat without light is still real.
abstract.cn: 没有光的热依然真实。

abstract.en: Passion burns by the same grammar as fire.
abstract.cn: 激情与火遵循同一套燃烧语法。

examples.en: The flame of the candle shook in the wind.
examples.cn: 蜡烛的火苗在风里摇晃。

examples.en: Dry wood burst into flames.
An old flame of hers called last night.
examples.cn: 她的旧情人昨晚打来电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: flame 源自拉丁语 flamma（火焰），与 flare（吹）同源，核心是「被吹旺的火」。

root: 源自拉丁语 flamma（火焰），与 flare（吹）同源，核心义「燃起的亮火」。

sensesIntro.en: Flame means a tongue of fire, a strong fire, passion, or to burn brightly.
sensesIntro.cn: flame 意为火苗、烈火、激情或熊熊燃烧。

core.en: Bright burning gas with heat and light.
core.cn: 带光带热的明亮燃烧气体。

branches.en: The visible tongue of a fire.
A whole body of burning material.
Heat felt as strong emotion.
branches.cn: 以强烈情感形式感受到的热。

branches.en: The action of giving bright fire.
Fire and feeling share the image of heat.
branches.cn: 火与情感共享热的意象。

intro.en: Flame belongs to the Latin flamm- family of burning words.
intro.cn: flame 属于拉丁语 flamm- 这一表示燃烧的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin flamma and flammare are the direct ancestors of the flaming family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flamma 与 flammare 是这一词族的直接来源。

items.example: A flaming torch lit the way.
items.exampleCN: 一支燃烧的火把照亮了路。

items.example: Keep the gas away from flammable things.
The suit is made of nonflammable cloth.
items.exampleCN: 这套衣服用不易燃的布料做成。

items.example: The pan has a flameproof handle.
The chef made a flambe dessert.
items.exampleCN: 厨师做了一道火焰甜点。

latinEntries.example: Flamma is the Latin word for flame.
latinEntries.exampleCN: flamma 是拉丁语中的「火焰」。

latinEntries.example: Flammare meant to kindle a fire.

definition_zh: 闪光；一瞬间；闪现；新闻快讯
definition_en: a sudden bright light, a very short moment, to shine briefly, or a short news report
core_image: 相机闪光灯在暗处炸开一团白光
scene: 相机闪光灯在黑暗里突然亮了一下。The camera flash went off in the dark.
sceneCN: 这里 flash 是「闪光」（第 1 个义项）；句意：相机闪光灯在黑暗里突然亮了一下。

senses.title: Sudden light
senses.definition: a sudden bright burst of light
senses.definitionCN: 突然爆发的明亮光线
senses.example: The camera flash went off in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 相机闪光灯在黑暗里亮了一下。
senses.why: The word imitates the suddenness of light.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿了光突然出现的样子。

senses.title: Short moment
senses.definition: an extremely short period of time
senses.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间
senses.example: In a flash the room was empty.
senses.why: A flash of light lasts only an instant.
senses.whyCN: 一道闪光只持续一瞬。

senses.title: Shine briefly
senses.definition: to shine or appear for a very short time
senses.definitionCN: 短暂地发亮或出现
senses.example: A light flashed across the window.
senses.why: The noun became a verb of brief shining.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为短暂发亮的动词。

senses.title: News bulletin
senses.definition: a short urgent news report
senses.definitionCN: 简短而紧急的新闻报道
senses.example: We heard a news flash on the radio.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在收音机里听到一条快讯。
senses.why: News that arrives suddenly is like a flash of light.
senses.whyCN: 突然传来的新闻就像一道闪光。

intro.en: Flash arose in Middle English, probably imitating a sudden splash or burst of light.
intro.cn: flash 出现于中古英语，可能模仿突然的溅射或光爆。

items.en: The word may echo a sudden splash or strike.
items.cn: 这个词可能模仿突发的溅射或撞击声。

items.en: Flashen meant to dash, splash, or shine.
items.cn: flashen 意为猛冲、溅出或发亮。

items.en: A flash became a sudden burst of light.
items.cn: flash 指突然爆发的一道光线。

items.en: Photography gave the flash a lamp that fires briefly.
items.cn: 摄影术让 flash 指瞬时发亮的灯。

items.en: Flash also names a very short moment or a news bulletin.
items.cn: flash 也指极短的瞬间或新闻快讯。

note.en: Flash is compared with similar-looking words and with words for brief light.
note.cn: 把 flash 与形近词以及表示短暂光亮的词作比较。

entries.definition: the soft body of a person
to become red or wash out

normalIntro.en: Flash is a burst, then the instant it fills, then any signal that arrives suddenly.
normalIntro.cn: flash 先是一团光爆，再指它占满的那一瞬，最后指突然到来的讯号。

normal.en: A flash lit the dark room.
normal.cn: 一道闪光照亮了黑暗的房间。

normal.en: He was gone in a flash.
Headlights flashed in the distance.
The radio gave a news flash.
A flashback returns to the past.

abstract.en: Light that lasts one instant still changes the dark.
abstract.cn: 只存在一瞬的光也能改变黑暗。

abstract.en: Attention moves in flashes, not in lines.
abstract.cn: 注意力以闪光的方式移动，而非直线。

abstract.en: What arrives suddenly feels more real.
abstract.cn: 突然到来的东西显得更真实。

examples.en: The camera flash went off in the dark.
examples.cn: 相机闪光灯在黑暗里亮了一下。

examples.en: A flash of lightning lit the sky.
The news flashed across the screen.

dict_mnemonic.text: flash 是中古英语的拟声词，模仿光与物的突然迸发，核心义「一瞬间炸开」。

root: 拟声来源，中古英语 flashen 表「猛冲、溅出、发亮」，核心画面是「突然迸发」。

sensesIntro.en: Flash means a burst of light, a brief moment, a sudden shine, or a news bulletin.
sensesIntro.cn: flash 意为一道闪光、一瞬间、短暂发亮或新闻快讯。

core.en: A burst that exists for an instant.
core.cn: 只存在一瞬的迸发。

branches.en: A sudden burst of brightness.
The smallest slice of time.
A brief shining or appearing.
News arriving like a burst of light.
branches.cn: 像光爆一样到来的新闻。

branches.en: The noun and verb share the same burst.
branches.cn: 名词与动词共享同一次迸发。

intro.en: Flash is an English word that builds compounds for cameras, lamps, and memory.
intro.cn: flash 是英语本土词，能与相机、灯具和记忆构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Flash has no Latin ancestor; Latin fulgur, lightning, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flash 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 fulgur（闪电）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The film uses a short flashback.

items.meaning: a bulb that makes a flash
items.example: The old camera needs a flashbulb.
items.exampleCN: 这台旧相机需要闪光灯泡。

items.example: Take a flashlight into the cave.

definition_zh: 平的；公寓；平淡的；瘪了的
definition_en: having an even surface, an apartment, dull without energy, or deflated
core_image: 一块刚擀开的桌面，摸不到一点起伏
scene: 我们在一间小小的公寓里住了两晚。We stayed two nights in a small flat.
sceneCN: 这里 flat 是「公寓」（第 2 个义项）；句意：我们在一间小小的公寓里住了两晚。

senses.title: Level
senses.definition: having a surface without slopes or bumps
senses.definitionCN: 表面没有倾斜或凸起的
senses.example: The land is flat for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地平坦绵延数英里。
senses.why: This is the literal physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的物理义项。

senses.title: Apartment
senses.definition: a set of rooms for living on one floor
senses.definitionCN: 位于同一层的一套住所
senses.example: We stayed two nights in a small flat.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在一间小公寓里住了两晚。
senses.why: A flat is one level of a building, hence a dwelling.
senses.whyCN: 公寓占楼的一层，因此用「平」来表示。

senses.title: Dull
senses.definition: lacking interest, energy, or variation
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏趣味、活力或变化的
senses.example: The party felt flat after the speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 讲话结束后聚会变得平淡。
senses.why: Something without peaks seems level and lifeless.
senses.whyCN: 没有起伏的东西显得平坦而无生气。

senses.title: Deflated
senses.definition: having lost air, as a tyre
senses.definitionCN: 像轮胎一样失去空气的
senses.example: The tyre went flat on the way home.
senses.why: A deflated tyre is pressed flat to the ground.
senses.whyCN: 瘪胎被压平贴在地面上。

intro.en: Flat comes from Old Norse flatr, related to Old English flet, a floor or dwelling.
intro.cn: flat 源自古诺尔斯语 flatr，与古英语 flet（地板、住所）相关。

items.en: Flatr meant level or spread out.
items.cn: flatr 意为平坦的、铺开的。

items.en: Flat named a level surface.
items.cn: flat 指平坦的表面。

items.en: A flat became a dwelling on one floor.
items.cn: flat 开始指一层的住所。

items.en: The word described dull or lifeless things.
items.cn: 这个词用来形容平淡无生气的事物。

items.en: A flat tyre meant one emptied of air.
items.cn: flat tyre 指被放空空气的轮胎。

note.en: Flat is compared with similar-looking words and with words for level surfaces.
note.cn: 把 flat 与形近词以及表示平整表面的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flat is one even plane: land, a floor to live on, a mood without peaks, a tyre without air.
normalIntro.cn: flat 就是一个平面：土地、居住的一层、没有起伏的情绪、没有气的轮胎。

normal.en: The road is flat and straight.
They rent a flat in town.
normal.cn: 他们在城里租了一套公寓。

normal.en: The joke fell flat.
We changed the flat tyre.
Flatten the dough with a roller.

abstract.en: A flat surface hides how much ground it covers.
abstract.cn: 平坦的表面看不出它覆盖了多远。

abstract.en: Without hills, a landscape has no surprises.
abstract.cn: 没有山丘，风景就少了惊喜。

abstract.en: Even a flat road still leads somewhere.
abstract.cn: 即使平坦的路也通向某处。

examples.en: We stayed two nights in a small flat.
examples.cn: 我们在一间小公寓里住了两晚。

examples.en: The land is flat for miles.
examples.cn: 这片土地平坦绵延数英里。

examples.en: The tyre went flat on the way home.

dict_mnemonic.text: flat 源自古诺尔斯语 flatr（平坦），核心义「平」，由平的地面引申为一层公寓、平淡与瘪掉。

root: 源自古诺尔斯语 flatr（平坦、铺开），核心义「没有起伏的平面」。

sensesIntro.en: Flat means level, an apartment, dull, or emptied of air.
sensesIntro.cn: flat 意为平坦的、公寓、平淡的或瘪了的。

core.en: A surface with no height or dip.
core.cn: 没有高低起伏的表面。

branches.en: Ground without slopes or bumps.
branches.cn: 没有坡度和凸起的地面。

branches.en: One level of a building to live on.
A mood or event without peaks.
branches.cn: 没有起伏的情绪或事件。

branches.en: A tyre pressed flat by lost air.
The level surface and the dwelling share one word.
branches.cn: 平面与住宅共用一个词。

intro.en: Flat is a Germanic word that builds words for pressing, manner, and shared homes.
intro.cn: flat 是日耳曼语词，能构成表示压平、方式和合住的词。

latinIntro.en: Flat has no Latin ancestor; Latin planus, level, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flat 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 planus（平的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: This road is flatter than that one.
It is the flattest field here.

items.meaning: in a firm or dull way

items.example: The flatness of the plain surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 平原的平坦让我们惊讶。

items.meaning: a person who shares a flat

definition_en: the taste of food or drink, a distinctive quality, or to give food a particular taste
core_image: 一勺热汤在舌尖散开，先咸后鲜
scene: 这汤有淡淡的蒜味。The soup has a light flavour of garlic.
sceneCN: 这里 flavour 是「味道」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这汤有淡淡的蒜味。

senses.title: Taste
senses.definition: the taste that food or drink has in the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 食物或饮料在口中的味道
senses.example: The soup has a light flavour of garlic.
senses.why: This is the everyday sense used for food and drink.
senses.whyCN: 这是描述饮食时最日常的义项。

senses.title: Character
senses.definition: a distinctive quality or atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 某种独特的气质或氛围
senses.example: The old town keeps a flavour of the past.
senses.exampleCN: 老城保留着过去的风味。
senses.why: Taste became a metaphor for character.
senses.whyCN: 味道被隐喻为事物的特色。

senses.title: Kind
senses.definition: a particular kind of food with a certain taste
senses.definitionCN: 带有特定味道的一类食品
senses.example: They sell ten flavours of ice cream.
senses.exampleCN: 他们卖十种口味的冰淇淋。
senses.why: Each kind of ice cream is named by its taste.
senses.whyCN: 每种冰淇淋都按味道来命名。

senses.title: To season
senses.definition: to give food a particular taste
senses.definitionCN: 给食物增添特定味道
senses.example: She flavoured the sauce with lemon.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb of adding taste.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为添加味道的动词。

intro.en: Flavour comes from Old French flaor, probably from a Latin word for smell or blowing.
intro.cn: flavour 源自古法语 flaor，可能出自拉丁语中表示气味或吹拂的词。

items.en: Flare meant to blow or breathe out.
items.cn: flare 意为吹出或呼出。

items.en: Flator named a smell carried in the air.
items.cn: flator 指空气中传来的气味。

items.en: Flaor meant smell or taste.
items.cn: flaor 意为气味或味道。

items.en: Flavour named the taste of food.
items.cn: flavour 指食物的味道。

items.en: The word extended to atmosphere and character.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到氛围与特色。

note.en: Flavour is compared with similar-looking words and with words for taste and smell.
note.cn: 把 flavour 与形近词以及表示味道和气味的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flavour is what the tongue reports and what an atmosphere quietly carries.
normalIntro.cn: flavour 既是舌头报告的味道，也是氛围悄悄携带的特色。

normal.en: This tea has a floral flavour.
The town has a old flavour.
Which flavour do you want?
Lemon flavours the sauce.
A flavour enhancer adds taste.

abstract.en: Taste is memory arriving through the tongue.
abstract.cn: 味道是经由舌头抵达的记忆。

abstract.en: A place has a flavour no menu can list.
abstract.cn: 一个地方的风味是菜单列不出的。

abstract.en: Small additions change the whole dish.
abstract.cn: 少许添加就能改变整道菜。

examples.en: The soup has a light flavour of garlic.
They sell ten flavours of ice cream.
examples.cn: 他们卖十种口味的冰淇淋。

examples.en: She flavoured the sauce with lemon.

dict_mnemonic.text: flavour 经古法语 flaor 上溯到拉丁语 flare（吹），本义「随空气传来的气味」，后专指味道与风味。

root: 源自古法语 flaor（气味、味道），与拉丁语 flare（吹）相关，核心义「空气带来的气味」。

sensesIntro.en: Flavour means the taste of food, a distinctive character, a kind of food, or to season.
sensesIntro.cn: flavour 意为食物的味道、独特风味、某种口味或给食物调味。

core.en: A taste or character carried by something.
core.cn: 由某物承载的味道或特色。

branches.en: What the tongue reports.
The atmosphere a place keeps.
A food named by its taste.
branches.cn: 以味道命名的一类食品。

branches.en: The act of adding taste.
Taste and character share the same word.
branches.cn: 味道与特色共用一个词。

intro.en: Flavour builds a small family of tastes, tools, and qualities.
intro.cn: flavour 构成一个关于味道、用品和性质的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Flavour has no direct Latin noun; Latin flare, to blow, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: flavour 没有直接的拉丁语名词；拉丁语 flare（吹）是更远的词根。

items.exampleCN: 这是一道味道浓郁的菜。
标签列出了所有调味成分。

latinEntries.example: Flare gave the word its sense of air.
latinEntries.exampleCN: flare 赋予这个词空气的意味。

definition_en: to run away from danger or a place, or to avoid something unpleasant
core_image: 一个人转身冲出门口，连头也不回
scene: 小偷在警察赶到前逃走了。The thief fled before the police arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 flee 是「逃跑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小偷在警察赶到前逃走了。

senses.title: Run from danger
senses.definition: to run away quickly from danger
senses.definitionCN: 迅速逃离危险
senses.example: The thief fled before the police arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷在警察赶到前逃走了。
senses.why: This is the core sense of physical escape.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体逃离的核心义项。

senses.title: Leave a place
senses.definition: to leave a place quickly because it is unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 因不安全而迅速离开某地
senses.example: Thousands fled the flooded town.
senses.exampleCN: 数千人逃离了被淹的城镇。
senses.why: The danger is a place rather than a pursuer.
senses.whyCN: 危险来自地点而非追捕者。

senses.title: Avoid
senses.definition: to avoid something unpleasant or difficult
senses.definitionCN: 回避令人不快或困难的事物
senses.example: He fled from the question.
senses.why: The idea of escape extends from danger to discomfort.
senses.whyCN: 逃离的概念从危险扩展到不适。

intro.en: Flee is a native Germanic verb, Old English fleon, meaning to fly or run away.
intro.cn: flee 是日耳曼语本族动词，古英语 fleon 意为飞走或逃开。

items.en: Fleuhan meant to fly or escape.
items.cn: fleuhan 意为飞走或逃脱。

items.en: Fleon meant to take flight from danger.
items.cn: fleon 意为逃离危险。

items.en: Fleen kept the same sense of running away.
items.cn: fleen 保留了逃跑的意思。

items.en: Flee stayed a strong verb with fled as its past.
items.cn: flee 保持强变化，过去式为 fled。

items.en: The verb also came to mean avoiding a topic.
items.cn: 这个词也引申为回避话题。

note.en: Flee is compared with similar-looking words and with words for escape.
note.cn: 把 flee 与形近词以及表示逃跑的词作比较。

entries.definition: to get away from a place

normalIntro.en: Flee is flight on foot: the body leaves first and the reason comes later.
normalIntro.cn: flee 是用脚完成的飞走：身体先离开，理由随后才到。

normal.en: They fled the burning house.
normal.cn: 他们逃离了燃烧的房子。

normal.en: The bird fled at our approach.
normal.cn: 鸟在我们靠近时飞走了。

normal.en: He fled from the crowded room.
normal.cn: 他从拥挤的房间逃了出去。

normal.en: Many fled the war.
She fled rather than answer.

abstract.en: Running away is also a way of deciding.
abstract.cn: 逃跑也是一种做决定的方式。

abstract.en: Some dangers follow the one who flees.
abstract.cn: 有些危险会跟着逃跑的人。

abstract.en: The fastest answer is sometimes distance.
abstract.cn: 有时最快的回答就是拉开距离。

examples.en: The thief fled before the police arrived.
examples.cn: 小偷在警察赶到前逃走了。

examples.en: Thousands fled the flooded town.
examples.cn: 数千人逃离了被淹的城镇。

examples.en: He fled from the question.

dict_mnemonic.text: flee 源自古英语 fleon（飞走、逃开），核心义「用最快的速度离开危险」。

root: 源自古英语 fleon（飞走、逃开），与「飞」同族，核心义「迅速离开」。

sensesIntro.en: Flee means to run from danger, to leave an unsafe place, or to avoid something.
sensesIntro.cn: flee 意为逃离危险、离开不安全的地方或回避某事。

core.en: To leave fast because staying is dangerous.
core.cn: 因留下危险而迅速离开。

branches.en: Running from a threat.
Leaving a dangerous place.
Backing away from a hard question.
The threat and the place are often the same.
branches.cn: 威胁与地点常常是同一个。

branches.en: Physical escape becomes emotional escape.
branches.cn: 身体逃离变成情感回避。

intro.en: Flee has a small native family built on flight and escape.
intro.cn: flee 的词族不大，围绕飞行与逃脱构成。

latinIntro.en: Flee has no Latin ancestor; Latin fugere, to flee, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flee 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 fugere（逃跑）只是语义对应词。

items.example: He flees at the sight of fire.
The fleeing crowd filled the street.
items.exampleCN: 逃跑的人群挤满了街道。

items.example: The refugee found a new home.

items.meaning: a person who has run off

definition_en: a group of ships, vehicles, or aircraft, or fast in movement
core_image: 一排同型船只在海面整齐前行
scene: 一支渔船队清晨驶出港口。The fishing fleet left the harbour at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 fleet 是「船队」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一支渔船队清晨驶出港口。

senses.title: Group of ships
senses.definition: a group of ships sailing or fighting together
senses.definitionCN: 一起航行或作战的一群船只
senses.example: The fishing fleet left the harbour at dawn.
senses.why: This is the oldest and central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最核心的义项。

senses.title: Group of vehicles
senses.definition: a group of vehicles or aircraft owned or moving together
senses.definitionCN: 归同一方所有或一起行动的一群车辆或飞机
senses.example: The company runs a fleet of buses.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司运营一支公交车队。
senses.why: The ship sense extended to any group that moves together.
senses.whyCN: 船队的义项扩展到任何一起行动的群体。

senses.title: Fast
senses.definition: moving quickly, used mainly in literary English
senses.definitionCN: 移动迅速的，主要用于文学语言
senses.example: The fleet deer outran the dogs.
senses.why: A separate Old Norse word for swift joined the same spelling.
senses.whyCN: 另一个表示迅捷的古诺尔斯语词合并进了同一拼写。

senses.title: Pass swiftly
senses.definition: to pass quickly, as time does
senses.definitionCN: 像时间一样迅速流逝
senses.example: The summer fleeted by.
senses.why: The idea of speed became a verb of passing time.
senses.whyCN: 速度的概念转化为时间流逝的动词。

intro.en: Fleet joins an Old English word for ship with an Old Norse word for swift.
intro.cn: fleet 把古英语中表示船的词与古诺尔斯语中表示迅捷的词合在了一起。

items.en: Fleot meant a ship or a float.
items.cn: fleot 意为船或漂浮物。

items.en: Fleotan meant to float or swim.
items.cn: fleotan 意为漂浮或游动。

items.en: Fljotr meant swift and gave the adjective.
items.cn: fljotr 意为迅捷，提供了形容词义。

items.en: Fleet named a group of ships.
items.cn: fleet 指一群船只。

items.en: The word extended to cars, buses, and aircraft.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到汽车、公交和飞机。

note.en: Fleet is compared with similar-looking words and with words for groups of vehicles.
note.cn: 把 fleet 与形近词以及表示车船群体的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A fleet is many hulls moving as one, and the same word once meant swift.
normalIntro.cn: fleet 是许多船体作为一个整体移动，同一个词还曾表示迅捷。

normal.en: The fleet sailed at dawn.
The firm owns a fleet of vans.
normal.cn: 公司拥有一支厢式货车队。

normal.en: A fleet horse won the race.
The years fleet past.
A fleeting glance is very short.

abstract.en: Many separate ships become one force when they sail together.
abstract.cn: 许多单独的船一起航行时成为一股力量。

abstract.en: Speed is measured best against something still.
abstract.cn: 速度最好相对于静止之物来衡量。

abstract.en: What passes quickly is remembered in outlines.
abstract.cn: 快速消逝之物只留下轮廓被记住。

examples.en: The fishing fleet left the harbour at dawn.
The company runs a fleet of buses.
examples.cn: 这家公司运营一支公交车队。

examples.en: The fleet deer outran the dogs.

dict_mnemonic.text: fleet 由古英语 fleot（船）与古诺尔斯语 fljotr（迅捷）汇合，兼有「船队」与「快速」两义。

root: 古英语 fleot（船、漂浮物）与古诺尔斯语 fljotr（迅捷）汇合，核心义「成群的船」与「快」。

sensesIntro.en: Fleet means a group of ships, vehicles, or aircraft, or fast in movement.
sensesIntro.cn: fleet 意为船队、车队、机群，或移动迅速。

core.en: A group moving together, or moving fast.
core.cn: 一起移动的群体，或移动得很快。

branches.en: Ships sailing as one body.
branches.cn: 作为一个整体航行的船。

branches.en: Vehicles or aircraft in one group.
branches.cn: 同一群体中的车辆或飞机。

branches.en: A literary word for swift.
Time passing like a fast ship.
The group and the speed share one spelling.
branches.cn: 群体与速度共用一个拼写。

intro.en: Fleet builds a compact family around ships and swiftness.
intro.cn: fleet 围绕船只与迅捷构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Fleet has no Latin ancestor; Latin classis, a fleet, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fleet 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 classis（舰队）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 我们看见一个一闪而过的影子。

items.example: The deer is known for fleetness.

definition_en: the soft tissue of a body, the edible part of an animal, or the soft part of a fruit
core_image: 刀切下去，露出湿润的粉色肌理
scene: 刀切开了果肉。The knife cut through the flesh of the fruit.
sceneCN: 这里 flesh 是「果肉」（第 2 个义项）；句意：刀切开了果肉。

senses.title: Body tissue
senses.definition: the soft part of a body between skin and bone
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤与骨骼之间的柔软部分
senses.example: The wound went deep into the flesh.
senses.why: This is the basic anatomical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的解剖学义项。

senses.title: Fruit pulp
senses.definition: the soft edible part of a fruit
senses.definitionCN: 水果柔软可食的部分
senses.example: The knife cut through the flesh of the fruit.
senses.why: The soft body of a fruit resembles soft body tissue.
senses.whyCN: 水果柔软的部分类似柔软的身体组织。

senses.title: Physical body
senses.definition: the body as opposed to the spirit or mind
senses.definitionCN: 相对于精神或心灵的肉身
senses.example: The story speaks of the spirit and the flesh.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事谈论灵魂与肉体。
senses.why: Flesh came to stand for human physical nature.
senses.whyCN: flesh 进而代表人的肉体天性。

senses.title: To add detail
senses.definition: to add details to make an idea complete
senses.definitionCN: 添加细节使想法变得完整
senses.example: She fleshed out the plan with numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 她用数据充实了这个计划。
senses.why: Giving a plan flesh is giving it body.
senses.whyCN: 给计划加上「肉」就是让它有实体。

intro.en: Flesh is an old Germanic word, Old English flæsc, unchanged in meaning at its core.
intro.cn: flesh 是古老的日耳曼语词，古英语作 flæsc，核心含义几乎未变。

items.en: Flaiska named the soft parts of the body.
items.cn: flaiska 指身体柔软的部分。

items.en: Flæsc meant flesh or meat.
items.cn: flæsc 意为肉或肌肉。

items.en: Flesh kept both body and food senses.
items.cn: flesh 同时保留身体与食物两义。

items.en: The word named the soft part of fruit.
items.cn: 这个词开始指水果柔软的部分。

items.en: Flesh out became an idiom for adding detail.
items.cn: flesh out 成为「充实细节」的习语。

note.en: Flesh is compared with similar-looking words and with words for meat and pulp.
note.cn: 把 flesh 与形近词以及表示肉和果肉的词作比较。

entries.definition: the soft wet part of fruit

normalIntro.en: Flesh is the soft living middle: of a body, of a fruit, of a plan that needs detail.
normalIntro.cn: flesh 是柔软的生命中层：身体的、水果的、以及需要细节的计划。

normal.en: The flesh of the peach is sweet.
The thorn cut into his flesh.
They met him in the flesh.
Flesh out the idea with examples.
Flesh and blood ties the family together.

abstract.en: The soft part is where life is felt.
abstract.cn: 柔软之处正是生命被感知的地方。

abstract.en: To give flesh to an idea is to make it visible.
abstract.cn: 给想法以血肉就是让它可见。

abstract.en: Body and spirit argue in one word.
abstract.cn: 身体与精神在同一个词里争论。

examples.en: The knife cut through the flesh of the fruit.

items.en: The root meant to move through the air.

senses.title: Gather
senses.definition: to move or gather in large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 大批地移动或聚集
senses.example: Tourists flock to the beach in summer.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb of crowding together.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为成群聚集的动词。

intro.en: Flock is an Old English word, flocc, meaning a group or troop.
intro.cn: flock 是古英语词 flocc，意为群体或队伍。

items.en: Flocc meant a group of people or animals.
items.cn: flocc 指一群人或动物。

items.en: The word was used for sheep and birds.
items.cn: 这个词用于羊群和鸟群。

items.en: Flock also named a Christian congregation.
items.cn: flock 也指基督教会的会众。

items.en: The verb meant to gather in numbers.
items.cn: 动词形式意为成群聚集。

items.en: Flock is used for crowds of people.
items.cn: flock 用于形容人群。

note.en: Flock is compared with similar-looking words and with words for groups of animals.
note.cn: 把 flock 与形近词以及表示动物群体的词作比较。

entries.definition: to move with a quick motion

normalIntro.en: A flock is a group that moves as one: sheep, birds, or people drawn to the same place.
normalIntro.cn: flock 是作为一个整体移动的群体：羊、鸟，或被同一地方吸引的人。

normal.en: The flock moved down the hill.
Birds gathered in a large flock.
Fans flocked to the concert.
The shepherd counts his flock.
Sheep flock together for safety.
normal.cn: 羊群聚在一起以求安全。

abstract.en: A crowd can think like a flock.
abstract.cn: 人群的思维可以像羊群。

abstract.en: Following is easy inside a group.
abstract.cn: 在群体中跟随是容易的。

abstract.en: The shepherd knows the group by counting.
abstract.cn: 牧人通过计数来了解群体。

examples.en: A flock of sheep grazed on the hill.
A flock of geese crossed the sky.
Tourists flock to the beach in summer.

dict_mnemonic.text: flock 源自古英语 flocc（群体），核心义「聚成一群」，由羊群推及鸟群、人群与成群行动。

root: 源自古英语 flocc（群体、队伍），核心义「聚在一起的一群」。

sensesIntro.en: Flock means a group of sheep, birds, or people, or to gather in numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: flock 意为羊群、鸟群、人群，或成群聚集。

core.en: A group moving and staying together.
core.cn: 一起移动并待在一起的群体。

branches.en: Sheep kept and moved together.
Birds flying as one body.
branches.cn: 作为一个整体飞行的鸟。

branches.en: People gathered like animals.
The act of crowding toward a place.
Animal groups and human crowds share the word.
branches.cn: 动物群与人群共用一个词。

intro.en: Flock builds a small family around groups and gathering.
intro.cn: flock 围绕群体与聚集构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Flock has no Latin ancestor; Latin grex, a herd, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flock 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 grex（群）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The lamb stayed near its flockmate.

items.meaning: a record of a sheep flock
items.exampleCN: 农场主保存羊群谱系册。

definition_en: a large amount of water covering dry land, to cover an area with water, or a very large number of things
core_image: 河水漫过堤岸，把整条街变成浅海
scene: 暴雨淹没了低洼的村庄。The storm flooded the low village.
sceneCN: 这里 flood 是「淹没」（第 2 个义项）；句意：暴雨淹没了低洼的村庄。

senses.title: Overflowing water
senses.definition: a large amount of water that covers land that is usually dry
senses.definitionCN: 淹没通常干燥陆地的大量水
senses.example: The flood destroyed the bridge.
senses.why: This is the literal natural disaster.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的自然灾害。

senses.title: To cover with water
senses.definition: to cover an area with water
senses.definitionCN: 用水覆盖一片区域
senses.example: The storm flooded the low village.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨淹没了低洼的村庄。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of covering.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为覆盖的动词。

senses.title: Large amount
senses.definition: a very large number or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 数量极大的某物
senses.example: A flood of letters arrived.
senses.why: Too much water became a metaphor for too much of anything.
senses.whyCN: 水太多被隐喻为任何东西太多。

senses.title: Pour in
senses.definition: to arrive or enter in very large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的数量到达或进入
senses.example: Fans flooded into the stadium.
senses.why: A crowd moving like water is said to flood in.
senses.whyCN: 像水一样移动的人群被形容为涌入。

intro.en: Flood comes from Old English flod, related to flowan, to flow.
intro.cn: flood 源自古英语 flod，与 flowan（流动）相关。

items.en: The root meant a flowing of water.
items.cn: 这个词根意为水的流动。

items.en: Flod meant a mass of moving water.
items.cn: flod 指大量流动的水。

items.en: Flood named the great water of the Bible.
items.cn: flood 指《圣经》中的大洪水。

items.en: The verb meant to cover land with water.
items.cn: 动词形式意为用水淹没土地。

items.en: The word became a metaphor for great amounts.
items.cn: 这个词成为表示大量的隐喻。

note.en: Flood is compared with similar-looking words and with words for water and abundance.
note.cn: 把 flood 与形近词以及表示水和大量的词作比较。

entries.definition: the lower surface of a room
the red liquid in the body
the rise and fall of the sea

normalIntro.en: Flood is water leaving its place and taking too much space, then any mass that behaves the same way.
normalIntro.cn: flood 是水离开原位、占据过多空间，随后任何以同样方式泛滥的东西都叫 flood。

normal.en: The river flood covered the fields.
Rain flooded the streets.
A flood of complaints followed.
People flooded into the hall.
Floodgates hold back the water.

abstract.en: Water teaches that too much of a good thing moves things away.
abstract.cn: 水告诉我们，好东西太多会把一切冲走。

abstract.en: Attention can flood as easily as a river.
abstract.cn: 注意力可以像河流一样泛滥。

abstract.en: A channel is a promise that the flood will be guided.
abstract.cn: 渠道是洪水将被引导的承诺。

examples.en: The storm flooded the low village.
examples.cn: 暴雨淹没了低洼的村庄。

examples.en: The flood destroyed the bridge.
A flood of letters arrived.

dict_mnemonic.text: flood 源自古英语 flod（水流），与 flow 同根，核心义「漫出原位的水」，再引申为大量与涌入。

root: 源自古英语 flod（水流、洪水），与 flow 同根，核心义「漫出边界的大量水」。

sensesIntro.en: Flood means overflowing water, to cover land with water, a huge amount, or to pour in.
sensesIntro.cn: flood 意为洪水、淹没、大量或涌入。

core.en: Water or anything else exceeding its banks.
core.cn: 水或其他东西超出边界。

branches.en: Water covering dry land.
The act of covering with water.
A huge amount of anything.
A crowd entering like water.
Water and crowds both overflow their banks.
branches.cn: 水与人群都会漫过边界。

intro.en: Flood builds words for waters, barriers, and artificial light.
intro.cn: flood 构成表示洪水、屏障和人造光的词。

latinIntro.en: Flood has no Latin ancestor; Latin inundare, to flood, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flood 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 inundare（淹没）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: the act of covering with water

definition_en: the surface of a room that you walk on, a level of a building, to surprise greatly, or to knock someone down
core_image: 光脚踩在木地板上，听见空空的回声
scene: 她坐在客厅地板上。She sat on the living-room floor.
sceneCN: 这里 floor 是「地板」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她坐在客厅地板上。

senses.title: Walking surface
senses.definition: the flat surface of a room that you walk on
senses.definitionCN: 房间里供人行走的平面
senses.example: She sat on the living-room floor.
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Storey
senses.definition: one level of a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑中的一层
senses.example: Her office is on the third floor.
senses.why: Each level has its own floor surface.
senses.whyCN: 每一层都有自己的地面。

senses.title: To astonish
senses.definition: to surprise or confuse someone completely
senses.definitionCN: 使某人完全惊讶或不知所措
senses.example: The question floored me.
senses.why: Being floored is being knocked flat by surprise.
senses.whyCN: 被问倒就像被惊得趴在地上。

senses.title: To knock down
senses.definition: to hit someone so that they fall down
senses.definitionCN: 把某人打得倒下
senses.example: The punch floored him.
senses.why: The literal sense of sending someone to the floor.
senses.whyCN: 这是把人打到地板上的字面义。

intro.en: Floor comes from Old English flor, meaning the ground or a floor.
intro.cn: floor 源自古英语 flor，意为地面或地板。

items.en: The root named a flat ground surface.
items.cn: 这个词根指平坦的地面。

items.en: Flor meant the ground or a floor.
items.cn: flor 意为地面或地板。

items.en: Floor named the surface of a room.
items.cn: floor 指房间的地面。

items.en: Floor came to mean a level of a building.
items.cn: floor 开始指建筑的一层。

items.en: The verb meant to knock someone down.
items.cn: 动词形式意为把人击倒。

note.en: Floor is compared with similar-looking words and with words for ground and levels.
note.cn: 把 floor 与形近词以及表示地面和楼层的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Floor is the flat base of a room, one level of a building, and the ground you end on when knocked down.
normalIntro.cn: floor 是房间平坦的底面、建筑的一层，也是被击倒后落到的地方。

normal.en: The floor is cold in winter.
We live on the fourth floor.
The news floored everyone.
normal.cn: 这个消息震惊了所有人。

normal.en: He floored his opponent.
The dance floor was crowded.

abstract.en: A floor is a promise that there is a bottom.
abstract.cn: 地板是对「有底」的承诺。

abstract.en: Buildings count upward from a single surface.
abstract.cn: 建筑从一个平面开始向上计数。

abstract.en: Being floored is learning where the ground is.
abstract.cn: 被击倒就是认识地面在哪里。

examples.en: She sat on the living-room floor.
Her office is on the third floor.
The punch floored him.

dict_mnemonic.text: floor 源自古英语 flor（地面），核心义「脚下的平面」，由地板引申为楼层与「被打到地上」。

root: 源自古英语 flor（地面、地板），核心义「脚下平坦的底面」。

sensesIntro.en: Floor means the surface you walk on, a storey, to astonish, or to knock down.
sensesIntro.cn: floor 意为地板、楼层、使震惊或击倒。

core.en: The flat bottom surface of a space.
core.cn: 空间的平坦底面。

branches.en: The surface walked on indoors.
One level counted in a building.
Surprise that knocks you flat.
A blow that sends someone down.
The surface and the storey share one base.
branches.cn: 地板与楼层共享同一个底面。

intro.en: Floor builds words for boards, coverings, and building plans.
intro.cn: floor 构成表示地板条、铺装和建筑平面的词。

latinIntro.en: Floor has no Latin ancestor; Latin solum, ground, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: floor 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 solum（地面）只是语义对应词。

items.example: He was floored by the news.
The floorless hut was open to the ground.
items.exampleCN: 没有地板的小屋直接连着地面。
平面图显示有两间卧室。

definition_en: powder made from ground grain used for baking, or to cover something with such powder
core_image: 面粉从指缝漏下，在案板上堆成一座小雪山
scene: 面包师在案板上撒了些面粉。The baker dusted the board with flour.
sceneCN: 这里 flour 是「面粉」（第 1 个义项）；句意：面包师在案板上撒了些面粉。

senses.title: Ground grain
senses.definition: powder made by grinding grain, used for baking
senses.definitionCN: 把谷物磨成、用于烘焙的粉
senses.example: The baker dusted the board with flour.
senses.exampleCN: 面包师在案板上撒了些面粉。
senses.why: This is the everyday baking sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常烘焙的义项。

senses.title: To dust
senses.definition: to cover a surface with flour
senses.definitionCN: 在表面撒上面粉
senses.example: Flour the pan before adding batter.
senses.exampleCN: 倒入面糊前先在烤盘上撒粉。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of coating.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为覆盖的动词。

senses.title: Fine powder
senses.definition: a fine powder from other seeds or foods
senses.definitionCN: 由其他种子或食物磨成的细粉
senses.example: The recipe uses rice flour.
senses.why: The milling sense extends to other grains.
senses.whyCN: 研磨的义项扩展到其他谷物。

intro.en: Flour began as a spelling of flower, meaning the finest part of ground grain.
intro.cn: flour 最初是 flower 的拼写变体，指磨碎的谷物中最精细的部分。

items.en: Flos meant a flower, the best part.
items.cn: flos 意为花，也指最好的部分。

items.en: Flour meant flower or the finest part.
items.cn: flour 意为花或最精细的部分。

items.en: Flour named the finest meal of grain.
items.cn: flour 指谷物磨出的精细粉。

items.en: Flour became the usual word for ground grain.
items.cn: flour 成为表示面粉的常用词。

items.en: The spellings flour and flower split apart.
items.cn: flour 与 flower 的拼写分道扬镳。

note.en: Flour is compared with similar-looking words and with words for powders and grain.
note.cn: 把 flour 与形近词以及表示粉末和谷物的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flour is the flower of the grain: the finest powder left after grinding.
normalIntro.cn: flour 是谷物的「花」：研磨后留下的最细粉末。

normal.en: Add flour to the bowl.
Sift the flour twice.
Flour the table before kneading.
Rice flour is used in noodles.
The bread is made without flour.

abstract.en: Grinding turns a seed into something that can rise.
abstract.cn: 研磨把种子变成能发起来的东西。

abstract.en: The finest part of a grain became its own word.
abstract.cn: 谷物最细的部分成了独立的词。

abstract.en: Dust and bread begin as the same powder.
abstract.cn: 灰尘与面包都始于同样的粉。

examples.en: The baker dusted the board with flour.
examples.cn: 面包师在案板上撒了些面粉。

examples.en: Flour the pan before adding batter.
examples.cn: 倒入面糊前先在烤盘上撒粉。

examples.en: The recipe uses rice flour.

dict_mnemonic.text: flour 原是 flower 的变体，本义「谷物中最精细的部分」，后专指面粉，与 flower 分写。

root: 源自 flower（花、精华），本义「谷物磨出的精华细粉」，核心义「精细粉末」。

sensesIntro.en: Flour means ground grain for baking, to coat with flour, or a fine powder from other foods.
sensesIntro.cn: flour 意为烘焙用的面粉、撒面粉或其他食物磨成的细粉。

core.en: The finest powder of ground grain.
core.cn: 磨碎的谷物中最细的粉。

branches.en: Wheat ground into baking powder.
A surface dusted for baking.
Fine powder from other grains.
The powder and the dusting share one word.
branches.cn: 粉末与撒粉共用一个词。

branches.en: Any fine meal can be called flour.
branches.cn: 任何细磨谷物粉都能叫 flour。

intro.en: Flour builds a small family for baking and milling.
intro.cn: flour 围绕烘焙与研磨构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Flour goes back to Latin flos, a flower, through Old French flour.
latinIntro.cn: flour 经古法语 flour 上溯到拉丁语 flos（花）。

items.example: The fish is floured before frying.

items.exampleCN: 她烤了一个无面粉蛋糕。
他扛着一袋重重的面粉。

latinEntries.meaning: a flower or the best part
latinEntries.example: Flos is the Latin source of flour.
latinEntries.exampleCN: flos 是 flour 的拉丁语来源。

latinEntries.example: Florem passed through French as flour.

definition_zh: 繁荣；挥动；花饰；夸张动作
definition_en: to grow or succeed well, to wave something in the air, or a showy decorative movement
core_image: 乐手把琴弓向上一挑，收在一个漂亮的动作里
scene: 小生意在城里兴旺起来。The small business flourished in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 flourish 是「兴旺」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小生意在城里兴旺起来。

senses.title: Grow well
senses.definition: to grow strongly and healthily
senses.definitionCN: 茁壮而健康地生长
senses.example: The plants flourish in warm rain.
senses.exampleCN: 植物在暖雨中长得茂盛。
senses.why: This is the original sense of flowering.
senses.whyCN: 这是开花的本义。

senses.title: Succeed
senses.definition: to be successful or active
senses.definitionCN: 成功或活跃地发展
senses.example: The small business flourished in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 小生意在城里兴旺起来。
senses.why: A growing plant became a metaphor for success.
senses.whyCN: 生长的植物被隐喻为成功。

senses.title: Wave
senses.definition: to hold something up and move it about
senses.definitionCN: 举起某物并来回挥动
senses.example: He flourished the letter in triumph.
senses.why: A showy gesture is like a plant waving in the air.
senses.whyCN: 夸张的手势像植物在空中摆动。

senses.title: Decorative movement
senses.definition: a showy curve or gesture added for effect
senses.definitionCN: 为效果添加的夸张曲线或动作
senses.example: She signed with a flourish.
senses.exampleCN: 她签名时带了一个花饰。
senses.why: The noun names the flourish of a pen or hand.
senses.whyCN: 名词指笔或手的华彩动作。

intro.en: Flourish comes from Latin florere, to bloom, from flos, a flower.
intro.cn: flourish 源自拉丁语 florere（开花），来自 flos（花）。

items.en: Flos meant a flower.
items.cn: flos 意为花。

items.en: Florere meant to bloom or prosper.
items.cn: florere 意为开花或繁荣。

items.en: Florir meant to bloom or thrive.
items.cn: florir 意为开花或兴旺。

items.en: Flourish meant to bloom and succeed.
items.cn: flourish 意为开花与兴盛。

items.en: The word named a showy gesture or decoration.
items.cn: 这个词开始指夸张的动作或装饰。

note.en: Flourish is compared with similar-looking words and with words for thriving.
note.cn: 把 flourish 与形近词以及表示兴旺的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flourish is to bloom: plants, businesses, and hands all can do it.
normalIntro.cn: flourish 就是开花：植物、生意和手都能做出这个动作。

normal.en: The garden flourishes in spring.
Trade flourished after the war.
He flourished his hat.
She bowed with a flourish.
A flourish of trumpets opened the show.

abstract.en: What flourishes needs room, light, and patience.
abstract.cn: 繁茂需要空间、光和耐心。

abstract.en: A gesture can say what a word cannot.
abstract.cn: 一个动作能说出语言说不出的话。

abstract.en: The same word describes a plant and a pen.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既描述植物也描述笔。

examples.en: The small business flourished in the city.
examples.cn: 小生意在城里兴旺起来。

examples.en: The plants flourish in warm rain.
examples.cn: 植物在暖雨中长得茂盛。

examples.en: She signed with a flourish.
examples.cn: 她签名时带了一个花饰。

dict_mnemonic.text: flourish 源自拉丁语 florere（开花），核心义「像花一样展开」，由植物繁茂引申为事业兴旺与挥洒的动作。

root: 源自拉丁语 flos（花）与 florere（开花），核心义「像花一样盛开」。

sensesIntro.en: Flourish means to grow well, to succeed, to wave something, or a showy gesture.
sensesIntro.cn: flourish 意为繁茂、兴旺、挥动某物或夸张的花饰动作。

core.en: To open out like a flower.
core.cn: 像花一样展开。

branches.en: Plants growing strongly.
A business opening out.
A hand waving something grandly.
An added curve of style.
Plants and fortunes bloom alike.
branches.cn: 植物与运势以同样方式盛开。

intro.en: Flourish belongs to the Latin flor- family of flowers and blooming.
intro.cn: flourish 属于拉丁语 flor- 这一表示花与开花的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin flos and florere are the direct ancestors of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flos 与 florere 是该词族的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 这座镇子每年夏天都兴旺。

items.example: The flourisher waved a bright flag.
He writes in a florid style.

latinEntries.example: Flos is the root of the flor- family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: flos 是 flor- 词族的词根。

definition_en: to move steadily like water, or a steady movement or supply of something
core_image: 河水绕过石头，连成一条不停的线
scene: 河水缓缓流过石桥。The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 flow 是「流动」（第 1 个义项）；句意：河水缓缓流过石桥。

senses.title: Move like water
senses.definition: to move steadily in a stream
senses.definitionCN: 像水流一样稳定移动
senses.example: The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
senses.why: This is the core physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Steady movement
senses.definition: a continuous movement of people, goods, or information
senses.definitionCN: 人、货物或信息的持续移动
senses.example: The flow of traffic was heavy.
senses.why: Water became a model for any continuous movement.
senses.whyCN: 水成为任何持续运动的模型。

senses.title: Arise from
senses.definition: to come from a source
senses.definitionCN: 从某个来源产生
senses.example: Many problems flow from poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 许多问题源于计划不周。
senses.why: A river flows from its source, and so does a result.
senses.whyCN: 河流从源头流出，结果也从原因流出。

senses.title: Supply
senses.definition: the rate at which something is supplied
senses.definitionCN: 某物被供给的速率
senses.example: They measured the flow of water.
senses.why: The movement measured over time is a flow.
senses.whyCN: 随时间计量的运动就是流量。

intro.en: Flow comes from Old English flowan, a Germanic verb for moving like water.
intro.cn: flow 源自古英语 flowan，是日耳曼语中表示像水一样移动的动词。

items.en: The root meant to flow or stream.
items.cn: 这个词根意为流动或涌流。

items.en: Flowan meant to move like water.
items.cn: flowan 意为像水一样移动。

items.en: Flow also named a rising tide.
items.cn: flow 也指上涨的潮水。

items.en: The noun named a steady movement.
items.cn: 名词形式指稳定的运动。

items.en: The word extended to traffic, money, and ideas.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到交通、金钱和思想。

note.en: Flow is compared with similar-looking words and with words for moving liquid.
note.cn: 把 flow 与形近词以及表示液体运动的词作比较。

entries.definition: to flow, as a tap does

normalIntro.en: Flow is one continuous line of movement, of water, traffic, money, or causes.
normalIntro.cn: flow 是一条连续的运动线：水、交通、金钱或原因。

normal.en: The river flows to the sea.
Traffic flows better after the fix.
Cash flow keeps a business alive.
Good results flow from good habits.
The tide ebbs and flows.

abstract.en: Water teaches that movement needs a channel.
abstract.cn: 水告诉我们运动需要通道。

abstract.en: Blocked flow builds pressure.
abstract.cn: 被阻断的流动会积聚压力。

abstract.en: Every result has a source upstream.
abstract.cn: 每个结果在上游都有源头。

examples.en: The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
The flow of traffic was heavy.
Many problems flow from poor planning.
examples.cn: 许多问题源于计划不周。

dict_mnemonic.text: flow 源自古英语 flowan（流动），与 flood、fleet 同根，核心义「像水一样连续移动」。

root: 源自古英语 flowan（流动），核心义「连续不断的移动」。

sensesIntro.en: Flow means to move like water, a steady movement, a rate of supply, or to arise from.
sensesIntro.cn: flow 意为像水一样流动、持续运动、供给流量或源自某处。

core.en: Continuous movement along a course.
core.cn: 沿通道的连续运动。

branches.en: Water moving in a stream.
Traffic or goods in motion.
A result coming from a cause.
The measured rate of supply.
Rivers and reasons both have sources.

intro.en: Flow builds words for directions, instruments, and excess.
intro.cn: flow 构成表示方向、仪器和过量的词。

latinIntro.en: Flow has no Latin ancestor; Latin fluere, to flow, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flow 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 fluere（流）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The river flowed over the bank.
The flowing water cut the stone.
The outflow of money worried them.

definition_en: the colored bloom of a plant, to produce flowers, or the finest part of something
core_image: 一朵花在清晨打开，花瓣上还挂着露水
scene: 花园里的花开了。The flowers in the garden opened.
sceneCN: 这里 flower 是「花」（第 1 个义项）；句意：花园里的花开了。

senses.title: Bloom of a plant
senses.definition: the colored part of a plant that produces seeds
senses.definitionCN: 植物产生种子的彩色部分
senses.example: The flowers in the garden opened.
senses.why: This is the basic botanical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的植物学义项。

senses.title: Plant grown for blooms
senses.definition: a plant grown for its flowers
senses.definitionCN: 为观赏花而种植的植物
senses.example: She grows flowers on the balcony.
senses.why: The part stands for the whole plant.
senses.whyCN: 用部分代指整株植物。

senses.title: To bloom
senses.definition: to produce flowers
senses.definitionCN: 长出花朵
senses.example: The cherry trees flower in April.
senses.why: The noun became a verb of blooming.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为开花的动词。

senses.title: Finest part
senses.definition: the best or most valuable part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物中最好或最有价值的部分
senses.example: He is in the flower of his youth.
senses.why: The bloom is the peak of a plant's life.
senses.whyCN: 花是植物生命的高峰。

intro.en: Flower comes from Latin flos, flower, through Old French flour.
intro.cn: flower 经古法语 flour 上溯到拉丁语 flos（花）。

items.en: Flos meant a flower or the best part.
items.cn: flos 意为花或最好的部分。

items.en: Flour meant a flower or bloom.
items.cn: flour 意为花或花朵。

items.en: Flour named a bloom and the finest meal.
items.cn: flour 指花朵，也指最细的面粉。

items.en: Flower was respelled to show the plant sense.
items.cn: flower 被改拼以表示植物义。

items.en: Flower and flour became separate words.
items.cn: flower 与 flour 成为两个不同的词。

note.en: Flower is compared with similar-looking words and with words for blooms.
note.cn: 把 flower 与形近词以及表示花朵的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flower is the bright opening of a plant, the whole plant that bears it, and the best part of anything.
normalIntro.cn: flower 是植物明亮的绽放、承载它的整株植物，以及任何事物的精华。

normal.en: The flowers smell sweet.
She bought flowers for the table.
These trees flower in spring.
The garden is in flower.
Youth is the flower of life.

abstract.en: A flower is a plant's brief argument for beauty.
abstract.cn: 花是植物为美所作的短暂论证。

abstract.en: The best part is called the flower of the whole.
abstract.cn: 最好的部分被称为整体的花。

abstract.en: To bloom is to spend everything at once.
abstract.cn: 开花就是一次性倾尽所有。

examples.en: The flowers in the garden opened.
The cherry trees flower in April.
He is in the flower of his youth.

dict_mnemonic.text: flower 与 flour 同源，均出自拉丁语 flos（花），本义「精华」，一个指花，一个指面粉。

root: 源自拉丁语 flos（花、精华），核心义「植物盛开的精华部分」。

sensesIntro.en: Flower means a plant's bloom, a flowering plant, to bloom, or the finest part.
sensesIntro.cn: flower 意为花朵、花卉、开花或精华。

core.en: The opening bloom that holds a plant's best.
core.cn: 承载植物最佳部分的绽放。

branches.en: The colored seed-bearing part.
A plant kept for its blooms.
The act of opening into bloom.
The best part of a life or thing.
branches.cn: 生命或事物最好的部分。

branches.en: The bloom is both a part and a peak.

intro.en: Flower builds words for blooms, containers, and qualities.
intro.cn: flower 构成表示花朵、容器和性质的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin flos and florem are the direct ancestors of the flower family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flos 与 florem 是 flower 词族的直接来源。

items.example: The sunflower turns to the light.

latinEntries.example: Flos is the Latin word for flower.

latinEntries.exampleCN: florem 在法语中变成 flour。
